content.text: The cardinal principle underpinning every rule in this manual is simple: the ability to repay is non-negotiable; the willingness to repay is paramount. A high income with a poor repayment history is a worse risk than a moderate income with a spotless track record. Every parameter below must be read through this lens.

This document is binding on all credit officers, relationship managers, DSA channels, co-lending partners, and any third party involved in sourcing, processing, or decisioning personal loan applications.

Before any eligibility criterion is applied, every applicant must be correctly classified. Misclassification is a leading cause of policy violations and credit mis-pricing. The classification drives the entire downstream eligibility, income assessment, and documentation matrix.

rows.Sub-Category: NRI with NRE/NRO account in India

content.text: Policy Alert: Applicants cannot be reclassified by DSAs to avail a higher loan slab. Any reclassification must be documented, justified, and approved by a Level-2 Credit Officer.

Age is not merely a number — it is a proxy for earning horizon, financial maturity, and actuarial risk. The following rules have been calibrated based on the Company's internal vintage data spanning 1.2 million personal loan accounts.
The universal minimum age at the time of application is 21 completed years.
For salaried applicants, the minimum age of 21 ensures they have at minimum 1–2 years of work experience, which is independently verified.
For self-employed applicants, the minimum business vintage of 3 years means most self-employed borrowers will be aged 24+ in practice; the 21-year floor primarily covers inherited businesses.
Age to be established exclusively through OVDs (Officially Valid Documents): Aadhaar, PAN, passport, or birth certificate from a municipal authority. Affidavits are NOT acceptable.
In case of conflict between age on different OVDs, the Aadhaar-linked date of birth (as per UIDAI records) shall prevail.

Risk Expert's Note: Sub-25 borrowers have shown 2.3x higher early delinquency rates (EMI 1–3 defaults) in our portfolio versus the 30–45 age bracket. Apply additional income stability scrutiny for applicants below 25.

rows.Rationale: Aligns with typical private sector retirement
Professional income can extend well past 60
Business income tends to decline post-60
Pension is guaranteed income; risk is health

content.text: For pensioners, the maximum age at maturity of 72 years is an absolute hard stop. No exception process exists above this limit.

Joint applicants: if the primary applicant's age exceeds the maximum but a co-applicant meets age criteria and is a co-borrower (not merely a guarantor), the application may proceed under the co-applicant's age slab, subject to income re-assessment.
Age limits apply at the time of final credit sanction, not at enquiry or login stage. A borderline-age case must be sanctioned before the age limit is breached or declined.
Resident Indians (RIs) are eligible for all product variants without restriction.
Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) with active NRE / NRO accounts held with a scheduled commercial bank in India are eligible subject to the NRI-specific criteria in Section 9.
Persons of Indian Origin (PIO) holding OCI cards are treated at par with NRIs.
Foreign nationals, regardless of employment in India, are NOT eligible.
Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) who are also residents of India (RNOR status) are assessed as NRIs.
Minimum 1 year of continuous residence at current address. If current address tenure is less than 1 year, then previous address must show at least 2 years of residence.

Applicants with 3 or more address changes in the last 2 years trigger an enhanced residential verification (ERV) requirement; a field verification report (FVR) becomes mandatory irrespective of loan amount.

Applicants residing in rented accommodation: rental agreement must be registered or notarised. Self-declared rent receipts are acceptable only if cross-referenced with a bank statement showing rental debits.

Applicants residing in company-provided accommodation (CPA): a letter from the employer confirming housing provision is required. The loan repayment must be secured via NACH on a personal bank account, not a salary account subject to CPA deduction.
PO Box addresses, care-of addresses (C/O), and addresses identified as commercial premises only are not acceptable as residential addresses.

Risk Expert's Note: Address instability — specifically more than 2 address changes in 3 years — correlates with a 1.8x higher 90+ DPD rate in our portfolio. Field verification is non-negotiable for such profiles.

Aadhaar card is MANDATORY for all resident Indian applicants without exception. It serves as both identity and address proof. The Aadhaar must be linked to the applicant's active mobile number for OTP-based authentication.
PAN card is MANDATORY for all loans above INR 50,000 and for income tax verification. For loans at or below INR 50,000, Form 60 is acceptable only if the applicant does not have a PAN.
Passport serves as an alternative identity proof but does NOT substitute Aadhaar for address verification if the address is outdated.
Voter ID (EPIC) is acceptable as a secondary identity document but carries higher forgery risk; if submitted as primary, mandatory cross-check via the Election Commission's online voter portal.
Driving Licence (DL) is acceptable as identity + address proof; the DL must not be expired and must be issued by an RTO within India.
Step 1: Aadhaar e-KYC — OTP-based UIDAI API verification to confirm name, DOB, address, and mobile linkage. This must succeed before proceeding to the next step.

Step 2: PAN validation — PAN number verified against the Income Tax Department's Instant PAN validation API. Name on PAN must match the Aadhaar name (within permissible deviation of 2 characters for spelling variations).
Step 3: CKYC check — Search the CERSAI CKYC registry. If an existing CKYC record exists, retrieve and verify. If no record exists, create a new CKYC entry post-sanction.
Step 4: Facial Biometric — Mandatory for video KYC (VKYC). Liveness check via certified VKYC platform. The face must match the photo on the OVD submitted.

Step 5: Address Verification — Current residential address verified via utility bill (electricity/gas/water — not older than 3 months), registered rental agreement, or bank statement showing address (not older than 2 months).

Step 6: Negative List Check — Name, PAN, and Aadhaar to be run against the Company's internal negative list, RBI defaulter list, CIBIL's CAVE (Caution Advice & Verification Engine), and PMLA designated entities list.
Hard Rule: Any KYC step failure without satisfactory remediation is an automatic decline. There is no workaround for failed biometric or OTP authentication.

Employment eligibility for salaried applicants is assessed on three axes: employer quality, employment stability (vintage), and income regularity. Each axis is assigned a risk weight in the underwriting scorecard.
Employers are classified into four categories. This classification drives the minimum income threshold, maximum loan amount multiplier, and required documentation depth.

rows.Employer Type: Central / State Govt, Judiciary, Defence, PSU (Schedule A & B)
rows.Examples: IAS/IPS, RBI, BSNL, NHPC, ONGC, Army
rows.Underwriting Treatment: Highest income multiplier; lowest documentation burden; FOIR up to 60%

rows.Employer Type: Listed MNCs, Nifty 500 companies, Private banks / Insurance cos, Top 100 IT cos
rows.Examples: TCS, Infosys, HDFC Bank, Bajaj Finance, L&T
rows.Underwriting Treatment: High income multiplier; standard documentation; FOIR up to 55%

rows.Employer Type: Other listed companies (BSE/NSE), reputed unlisted firms with revenue > INR 100 Cr
rows.Underwriting Treatment: Moderate multiplier; ITR mandatory; FOIR up to 50%

rows.Employer Type: Small / medium unlisted companies, proprietorships paying salary, newly incorporated entities (< 3 years)
rows.Examples: Small shops, local contractors, startup companies
rows.Underwriting Treatment: Conservative multiplier; FVR mandatory; FOIR up to 45%; enhanced income scrutiny

content.text: CAT-4 employers require additional proof of business existence: GST filing copy, MCA master data, or trade licence. Salary paid in cash (without bank credit) is categorically not acceptable.
Employers that cannot be verified via MCA21, GST registry, or any official directory are treated as CAT-4 at minimum, or declined if verification is wholly impossible.

Applicants with multiple job changes (more than 3 employers in the last 3 years) are subject to a 'job-hopping overlay': FOIR threshold reduced by 5 percentage points, and a formal income re-assessment using average of last 2 ITRs.
Contractual employees, even at CAT-1 or CAT-2 employers, are classified as self-employed for income assessment purposes if their contract tenure is less than 12 months.
Any gap in employment exceeding 3 months in the past 2 years requires a written explanation from the applicant. The income during the gap period is excluded from income calculations.
Employees on loss-of-pay (LOP) leave during the income assessment period: the LOP days must be identified from the salary slip and the net income adjusted accordingly.
Salary must be credited to a scheduled commercial bank account; salary account must be in the applicant's sole name or joint name with family member.
Cash salary arrangements (with or without formal salary slips) are not eligible for personal loans above INR 50,000.
Salary credit date must be consistent across the last 6 months. Variation of more than 5 days in credit date across any 2 consecutive months requires explanation.
Split salary (partial bank credit + partial cash) is accepted only if the bank-credited portion alone satisfies the minimum income threshold.

Allowances that are part of CTC but not credited to the salary account (e.g., fuel allowance in vehicle, LTA in vouchers) are included in income only if evidenced in Form 16 under 'Exempt Allowances' — and only at 50% of their value.

Risk Expert's Note: The most common income inflation tactic we have encountered is inflating variable pay in salary slips while the actual bank credits are far lower. Always reconcile salary slips against bank statement credits to the rupee. Discrepancies above 10% must be investigated.

Self-employed income assessment is inherently more complex than salaried assessment because the income is not attested by a third party (employer). The underwriter must act as a quasi-auditor, verifying the plausibility, sustainability, and liquidity of the business income.
Professionals command better treatment due to regulated income structures, bar/council registration, and typically stable demand for their services.

rows.Income Assessment Base: Average net profit from ITR (last 2 years); clinic bank statement
Average net profit from ITR (last 2 years); practice account statement
Average net profit from ITR (last 2 years)
Average net profit from ITR (last 2 years); higher standard (5 years) due to income volatility
Average net profit from ITR (last 2 years); clinic bank statement

content.text: Minimum business vintage: 3 years of continuous operations, evidenced by GST registration (if turnover exceeds INR 20 lakhs / INR 10 lakhs for services in special category states), Udyam / MSME registration, or shop and establishment licence.

Business must be registered and operating at the address stated in the application. Dormant businesses, businesses registered at residential addresses without commercial activity, or shell entities are ineligible.

ITR for the last 2 consecutive assessment years is mandatory. The ITR must have been filed before the due date or within the condonation period. Belated returns filed under scrutiny are subject to additional verification.

CA-certified Profit & Loss account and Balance Sheet for the last 2 years are required. The CA must be a practising member of ICAI; the UDIN (Unique Document Identification Number) on the certificate must be verifiable on the ICAI UDIN portal.
Business bank statements for the last 12 months are required. The 12-month average monthly credit turnover must be at least 3x the proposed monthly EMI.
Businesses in negative sectors (casinos, tobacco manufacturing, illegal money lending, cryptocurrency exchanges, or sectors under RBI / SEBI scrutiny) are ineligible.
Businesses under IBC / NCLT proceedings, or where the applicant is a director or partner in an entity under such proceedings, are ineligible.

Risk Expert's Note: The most dangerous self-employed profile is a business with rapidly growing turnover (3x year-on-year) but no corresponding growth in net profit. This pattern often signals revenue inflation or the early stages of a Ponzi-like business structure. Always assess net profit margins, not just top-line revenue.
Sole proprietors: the business PAN and personal PAN may be the same; both must be verified. Business income flows to personal ITR under 'Business & Profession' head.

Partnership firms: the applicant must be an active, income-drawing partner (not a sleeping partner). The partnership deed must be registered and the applicant's share of profit must be verifiable from the firm's ITR.
LLP partners: similar treatment to partnership firms; the LLP must be registered with MCA and the applicant's designated partner status confirmed via MCA21.

In all business structures, the applicant's personal bank account and business bank account must be distinct. Mingling of funds (personal expenses paid from business account or vice versa) requires income re-assessment using blended cash flow analysis.

Income assessment is the core technical skill of credit underwriting. This section sets out the detailed methodology for deriving the 'eligible income' that is used for all loan eligibility and FOIR calculations. Understanding what to include, what to exclude, and what to discount is critical.

sections.heading: 6.1 Gross Income vs. Eligible Income: The Fundamental Distinction

content.text: The Company uses 'Eligible Net Monthly Income (ENMI)' — not gross CTC, not take-home salary — as the income base for all calculations. The derivation methodology differs by applicant class.
Step 1: Take the average of last 3 months' net salary credits to bank account (not salary slip — bank credit). This is the primary income figure.

Step 2: Add back the following allowances if they appear as deductions from gross salary on salary slip: Professional Tax (PT), voluntary PF contribution above statutory 12%, any loan recovery to the same NBFC/bank being applied to.

Step 3: Exclude from income: LTA (Leave Travel Allowance), medical reimbursements, performance bonuses if received irregularly (less than 8 months out of 12), joining bonuses, ex-gratia, and retention bonuses.

Step 4: Variable pay (including commissions, incentives) — include at 50% of the 12-month average if variable pay has been received in at least 9 of the last 12 months; exclude entirely if received in fewer than 9 months.
Step 5: Arrears, one-time payments, and backpay must be excluded from income calculations.
Overtime pay: include at 50% only if it has been consistently earned for the last 12 months and is evidenced in all 12 salary slips.

Average net profit as per ITR for the last 2 years. If year 2 income is lower than year 1 by more than 20%, use year 2 income only (declining trend principle — never use the higher of 2 years in a declining income profile).

Add back: depreciation (as per IT depreciation, not book depreciation), interest paid on business loans that are being repaid (these are already captured in FOIR), director's remuneration if the applicant is also a salaried director.
Exclude: income from speculative transactions (F&O, commodities), one-time asset sales, gifts, capital gains, and windfalls.

For proprietors with very high turnover but low net profit: investigate and assess whether the low profit reflects genuine business margins or tax avoidance. If the latter, a higher income may be considered but with a risk overlay.
Cash income (income not routed through bank) is excluded from eligible income for any loan above INR 2,00,000.

sections.heading: 6.2 Income from Other Sources — Treatment Policy

rows.Conditions for Inclusion: Registered lease deed; rent credited to bank account; rental income declared in ITR
Registered commercial lease; GST registration of tenant; rent credited to bank; declared in ITR
NOT eligible — exempt from income tax and unverifiable via standard bureau/ITR checks
Listed company dividends only; 24-month average; must be recurring, not one-time
Not eligible — capital-based, not income-based; not durable
Govt/Defence/PSU pension; credited to bank; pension payment order (PPO) required
Evidenced by TDS 26AS entries or Form 16A; 12-month average of last 2 years
Co-applicant must be blood relative or spouse; income verified independently as per their category

content.text: Agricultural income declared in ITR as 'exempt income' is a well-known mechanism for laundering cash income. Under no circumstances may agricultural income be admitted as eligible income or used to bridge an income shortfall.

sections.heading: 6.3 Minimum Eligible Net Monthly Income (ENMI) Thresholds

content.text: Risk Expert's Note: ENMI thresholds are minimum floors, not targets. A salaried applicant earning just above the floor with high FOIR is a worse risk than a self-employed applicant earning 2x the floor. Income sufficiency must be assessed holistically.

chapters.heading: SECTION 7: CREDIT BUREAU ASSESSMENT — DEEP DIVE

content.text: After two decades in retail credit, the author of this policy will state unequivocally: bureau analysis is the single most important underwriting tool available. No income verification, no field visit, and no reference check can substitute for a thorough reading of the credit bureau report. The bureau is the borrower's financial autobiography.
Primary bureau: CIBIL (TransUnion). Mandatory for all applications.
Secondary bureau: Experian India. Mandatory for loans above INR 5,00,000.
Tertiary bureau: CRIF Highmark. Required for any loan where CIBIL score is absent or below 650, or where applicant claims 'NH' (No Hit) status.

Bureau consent: Applicant must provide explicit written / digital consent for bureau pull. The consent must be specific to the loan product and current application; blanket or standing consents are not acceptable.
Bureau pull timing: Must be performed within 7 days of the credit decision. Applications where bureau data is older than 30 days at time of sanction require a fresh pull.

rows.Underwriting Treatment: Best pricing; highest multiplier; relaxed documentation
Higher pricing; DPD history must be clean in last 12 months
CAT-1/2 salaried only; FOIR cap reduced by 5pp; maximum tenor 36 months
Contact CRIF Highmark; if still no hit, decline

sections.heading: 7.3 Days Past Due (DPD) History — The Most Critical Parameter

content.text: DPD analysis must be conducted for EVERY active and closed account on the bureau report. The following rules govern DPD-based eligibility. These rules are ABSOLUTE and cannot be overridden by any other positive factor.
Zero tolerance — Automatic Decline: Any 90+ DPD (Non-Performing Asset level delinquency) on any secured or unsecured loan or credit card account in the last 36 months.
Zero tolerance — Automatic Decline: Any 60+ DPD in the last 18 months.
Zero tolerance — Automatic Decline: Any 30+ DPD in the last 12 months.

Conditional eligibility: 1–29 DPD (i.e., X DPD on bureau) in the last 12 months — maximum 2 instances; explanation required; FOIR reduced by 5pp; maximum loan amount capped at 50% of normal eligibility.
Historical DPD (beyond 36 months): DPD records older than 36 months are noted but do not trigger automatic decline; they are factored into the risk pricing overlay.
Settled accounts: any account showing 'Settled' status (meaning the full outstanding was not repaid) is treated as a 90+ DPD event regardless of when it was settled.

Written-off accounts: any write-off on the bureau — regardless of vintage — is an automatic decline. The applicant must obtain a 'No Dues Certificate' from the lender and clear the outstanding before re-applying.

Risk Expert's Note: Over the years, I have seen underwriters overlook a 'settled' account because it was old or the amount was small. This is a grave mistake. A settled account signals that the borrower, when under stress, chose negotiation over repayment. That behavioural trait does not expire.
Total number of open secured accounts (home loan, car loan, etc.) + unsecured accounts (personal loan, consumer loan) + credit cards: maximum 6 open accounts (excluding the proposed loan).
Open unsecured loan accounts (personal loans, consumer durable loans, gold loans treated as unsecured): maximum 3.

Credit card accounts: a credit card counts as an open account. For FOIR purposes, 5% of the combined credit limit across all cards is treated as a monthly obligation (irrespective of whether a balance is outstanding).
Total outstanding principal across all open unsecured accounts must not exceed 5x the applicant's ENMI at the time of application.
Accounts with current balance significantly higher than sanctioned limit (overlimit) indicate stress and trigger an additional FOIR buffer of 10pp.
Total hard enquiries in the last 6 months: if more than 5, the application is flagged as 'credit hungry' — a well-established predictor of financial distress.
5–7 enquiries in 6 months: eligible but FOIR capped at 45%; maximum tenor limited to 36 months.
More than 7 enquiries in 6 months: mandatory decline.
Enquiries from lenders in sectors such as payday lending, microfinance, and pawnbroking are weighted 2x in the enquiry count for risk assessment purposes.
A burst pattern (3+ enquiries in a single week from different lenders) is a fraud flag, not merely a credit risk flag, and triggers the fraud investigation protocol.
Minimum credit history vintage: 12 months for applicants aged 21–24; 24 months for applicants aged 25 and above.
An applicant with credit history of less than 12 months regardless of age is treated as NTC.

Product mix: applicants with a history of only credit cards (no instalment loans) may have an artificially high score. The underwriter must assess whether the applicant has experience managing EMI-based repayments.

Highest credit exposure: if the highest active individual loan outstanding is more than 10x the proposed loan, the applicant may not be in the NBFC's target segment; a cross-check with the lender's acquisition strategy is warranted.
Bureau report with more than 5 disputes ('Dispute' flag) is a fraud/litigation red flag and requires investigation before proceeding.
NTC applicants (CIBIL score = -1) are eligible under a ring-fenced underwriting framework with the following mandatory conditions:
NTC eligibility is restricted to CAT-1 and CAT-2 salaried applicants only.
Maximum loan amount: INR 3,00,000.
Maximum loan tenor: 24 months.
Minimum ENMI: 1.5x the standard minimum threshold for the applicant's employer category.
FOIR for NTC is capped at 40% (lower than standard, because we cannot verify true obligations without bureau history — there may be informal/family loans).
Salary account must be with a reputed scheduled commercial bank (not cooperative bank, RRB, or payments bank).
Employment confirmation letter mandatory; appointment letter and last 3 salary slips required.
Field verification mandatory regardless of loan amount.
NTC loans are automatically subject to 'Early Mortality Watch' — any default in EMI 1–3 triggers a full fraud investigation.

chapters.heading: SECTION 8: FOIR — FIXED OBLIGATIONS TO INCOME RATIO

content.text: FOIR is the most operationally important eligibility parameter because it determines whether the applicant can service the proposed EMI alongside all existing obligations. FOIR calculation errors are the most common cause of over-disbursement and early-stage delinquency.
Formula:   FOIR  =  (Total Monthly Fixed Obligations + Proposed EMI)  /  ENMI  x  100
Where 'Total Monthly Fixed Obligations' includes ALL of the following:
All active EMI obligations as appearing on the bureau report (home loans, car loans, education loans, personal loans, consumer durable loans, gold loans).
Credit card obligations: 5% of total combined credit limit across all cards, regardless of current outstanding.
Obligations not on bureau (known to the applicant — self-declared): personal borrowings from family, informal loans, chit fund obligations.
Advance EMI paid as security deposit to other lenders (these reduce future EMI burden but must be captured).
Rent obligations if paid via bank transfer: 50% of monthly rent is included in FOIR calculation (the other 50% is assumed to be recoverable as savings).
Child/spousal maintenance (alimony) if declared or evidenced by court order.

Obligations NOT seen on bureau but voluntarily disclosed by the applicant MUST be included. Any obligation later discovered that was not disclosed will be treated as a fraudulent misrepresentation and trigger immediate account review.

rows.Notes: Govt pension certainty justifies higher FOIR
Income more stable than Class C
Pension income is stable but health risk rises

rows.Standard FOIR Cap: FOIR cap reduced by 5pp vs standard

content.text: Risk Expert's Note: The FOIR threshold assumes that the remaining (non-FOIR) income covers food, clothing, shelter, healthcare, education, and incidental expenses. In low-income brackets (ENMI below INR 25,000), a 50% FOIR leaves only INR 12,500 for all living expenses — which is often insufficient in metro areas. The underwriter must apply a 'livability check': is the residual income after FOIR and basic expenses positive and meaningful?

Example: Salaried applicant, CAT-2, ENMI = INR 80,000; CIBIL = 735; existing obligations = home loan EMI INR 22,000 + car loan EMI INR 8,000 + credit card limit INR 2,00,000 (5% = INR 10,000). Total existing obligations = INR 40,000. Proposed loan EMI = INR 15,000.
FOIR = (40,000 + 15,000) / 80,000 = 55,000 / 80,000 = 68.75%  →  EXCEEDS 55% cap  →  INELIGIBLE at proposed EMI.

Maximum eligible proposed EMI = (55% x 80,000) – 40,000 = 44,000 – 40,000 = INR 4,000. At 14% interest and 48-month tenor, this implies a maximum eligible loan of approximately INR 1,65,000 — far below any standard minimum.
Decision: Decline or significantly restructure. This applicant is over-leveraged despite a good CIBIL score and high income.
The maximum eligible loan amount is the LOWER of: (a) the income multiplier-based limit, or (b) the FOIR-constrained limit. Both must be independently calculated and the lower of the two applied.
Minimum loan amount: INR 50,000 for all salaried categories; INR 1,00,000 for self-employed; INR 50,000 for pensioners.
Loan amounts must be disbursed in a single tranche. No staged disbursal for personal loans.
Tenor must never extend beyond the applicant's projected employment tenure (for salaried) or beyond the maximum age at maturity as defined in Section 2.
Short-tenor loans (12–24 months) attract higher EMI; the FOIR check must be conducted based on the actual EMI, not an assumed longer tenor.
NRI applicants must have a minimum 2-year NRE or NRO account with a scheduled commercial bank in India.
Minimum employment tenure overseas: 2 years in current employment; minimum total overseas experience: 3 years.
Co-applicant requirement: a resident Indian co-applicant (family member or spouse) is mandatory for all NRI personal loans above INR 5,00,000.

Income proof: last 3 months' overseas payslips or salary credit statement (consularised/apostilled OR provided with employer confirmation). Exchange rate conversion at FEDAI rate on the date of application.
Bank statement: last 12 months of NRE/NRO account statement with all inward remittances clearly evidenced.
Passport and visa validity: applicant's work permit / employment visa must not expire within the proposed loan tenor.
Countries with higher risk (as per FATF grey/blacklists): require Enhanced Due Diligence; L2 approval mandatory; maximum loan INR 10,00,000.
Disbursement: always to the NRE/NRO account in India. Never to an overseas account.
EMI collection: NACH mandate on NRE/NRO account in India. No overseas ECS.
Co-applicants are permitted for all personal loan products. The co-applicant must be a blood relative (spouse, parent, sibling, adult child) or a business partner.
Income of co-applicants can be clubbed with primary applicant income for ENMI and FOIR calculations, subject to independent income verification of the co-applicant.
The co-applicant's bureau report must be pulled independently. Any adverse bureau finding on the co-applicant triggers a review of the primary application.
The co-applicant's FOIR is calculated independently. The combined FOIR (primary + co-applicant obligations / combined ENMI) must satisfy the applicable threshold.

A co-applicant cannot be used solely to bridge a CIBIL score deficiency of the primary applicant. If the primary applicant's score is below 650, the application must be declined regardless of co-applicant score.
Third-party guarantors are accepted only in specific circumstances: NTC loans, CAT-4 salaried loans above INR 5,00,000, or loans with approved exceptions above the standard multiplier.
Guarantors must meet all eligibility criteria applicable to the borrower class (age, income, bureau, KYC).
The guarantor's obligations as guarantor will be reflected on the guarantor's own bureau report, affecting the guarantor's future borrowing capacity. This must be explicitly disclosed in writing.
Guarantors who are themselves existing borrowers of the Company with active personal loans are not eligible.
Applicants with an active personal loan from the Company (with 0 DPD for at least 12 consecutive months) are eligible for a Top-Up Loan subject to re-underwriting.
Top-up loans: maximum amount = original sanctioned loan amount minus current outstanding. New FOIR calculation must be performed including the top-up EMI.

Pre-approved offers: Credit Monitoring System (CMS) may generate pre-approved personal loan offers for existing customers meeting defined behavioural criteria (12 months DPD-free, income growth evidenced). Pre-approved offers still require fresh KYC and bureau at disbursal.
Applicants who have foreclosed a previous personal loan with the Company within 6 months of applying for a new one: minimum 6-month cooling-off period is mandatory before a new loan is sanctioned.

Applicants whose primary salary account is held with an NBFC-affiliated banking partner (under co-lending / account-linked arrangement): CIBIL score minimum may be relaxed by 10 points (e.g., 700 becomes 690) and processing fee reduced by 0.5%.
This relationship benefit does not extend to income multiplier, FOIR threshold, or age limit relaxations.
The following risk overlays are applied on top of the base eligibility criteria. They are grounded in 20 years of portfolio performance data across India's diverse geographic and economic landscape.

rows.Geography Type: Tier-2 Cities (state capitals, major industrial towns)
rows.Underwriting Overlay: No overlay for salaried; +5pp income threshold for self-employed
FVR mandatory for all loans; maximum tenor reduced by 12 months for self-employed

rows.Geography Type: High NPA geography (identified quarterly by Credit Risk team)
rows.Underwriting Overlay: CIBIL minimum +20 points; FOIR cap -5pp; FVR mandatory; maximum loan capped at 50% of standard cap
Moratorium on new disbursals in impacted pin codes during disaster period; new applications require 3-month waiting period post-disaster

sections.heading: 14.2 Sector / Industry Overlay for Salaried Applicants

content.text: Real estate developers, construction companies (not PSU civil works): CAT-3 at best, regardless of company size. Sector has historically high layoff rates during credit cycles.
Aviation industry employees: income volatility and cyclical job losses mandate FOIR cap of 45% and maximum tenor of 48 months.
Media & entertainment (project-based): classified as self-employed for income assessment if on contracts rather than permanent rolls.
Startups (< 3 years old, unlisted, VC-funded): classified CAT-4. ESOP income excluded. Cash salary only.
Banking, insurance, and financial services employees (other than the Company's own employees): no special overlay; standard criteria apply.

The following are ABSOLUTE, NON-WAIVABLE decline conditions. No credit officer, L2 authority, or business head has the power to override any of these criteria. Any approval in violation of these rules is ultra vires and will be treated as a policy breach.

rows.Decline Criterion: Active write-off or settlement on bureau report (any vintage)
90+ DPD on any account in the last 36 months
Applicant on RBI defaulter list, CIBIL CAVE, or Company internal blacklist
Applicant or guarantor under active IBC/NCLT insolvency proceedings
Declared wilful defaulter with any NBFC, bank, or financial institution
FOIR exceeds 65% after including proposed EMI (no exception process exists above 65%)
Age at loan maturity exceeds the maximum defined in Section 2
Aadhaar e-KYC or PAN validation fails and cannot be remediated
Applicant or associate entity on PMLA / FATF / UN sanctions / domestic terror financing list
More than 7 hard bureau enquiries in the last 6 months
Business existence < 3 years for self-employed applicants
Forged, tampered, or fabricated documents discovered at any stage
Income entirely from cryptocurrency, illegal, or unregulated activities
Loan purpose is speculative investment (stock market, F&O, crypto trading)
Applicant is a minor (below 18) or has been legally declared incompetent
Duplicate application — same PAN/Aadhaar already has an active loan application in the system

content.text: COMPLIANCE NOTE: Any attempt to structure an application to avoid triggering a mandatory decline criterion (e.g., splitting a loan across two applicants, falsely classifying an employer, or understating obligations) constitutes a fraudulent act by the facilitating employee and will be referred for disciplinary and legal action.

Exceptions to non-absolute criteria are a normal and expected part of underwriting. They exist to allow flexibility for compelling edge cases that the policy's bright-line rules may not fully capture. However, exceptions must be structured, documented, and genuinely rare.

rows.Exception Type: Age at maturity +2 years beyond cap
rows.Maximum Exception Allowed: Pensioner / Class B only; max +2 years

content.text: All exceptions must be recorded in the loan origination system (LOS) with a mandatory exception justification note of at least 100 words.
Exception approvals granted verbally or via informal communication (WhatsApp, call) are not valid; only LOS-recorded approvals count.
Exceptions are tracked monthly; if any credit officer's exception rate exceeds 15% of their approved volume, a mandatory review by the Chief Risk Officer is triggered.
Exception loans are flagged in the portfolio monitoring system and subject to 90-day accelerated surveillance post-disbursal.

content.text: Incomplete documentation is grounds for loan processing suspension. No sanction letter may be issued with pending mandatory documents. Post-sanction document collection is strictly prohibited except for the CKYC update confirmation.

chapters.heading: SECTION 18: SENIOR RISK EXPERT — CLOSING PRINCIPLES

content.text: Having underwritten personal loans through multiple credit cycles, I leave the team with the following principles that no policy document can fully capture:

Income is a lagging indicator. By the time income drops, the borrower is already in trouble. The leading indicator is behaviour — specifically, payment behaviour. A borrower who pays on time even when income is constrained is gold. A borrower who defaults even when income is comfortable is a ticking time bomb.
Documents lie; banks do not. Always reconcile every document claim against actual bank debits and credits. The bank account is the applicant's financial X-ray.

The purpose of the loan matters more than policy admits. A loan for medical emergency is different in kind from a loan to repay another loan. Ask. Document it. Assess whether the purpose suggests a sustainable financial situation or a deepening crisis.

Geography is fate in retail credit in India. A teacher in Chandigarh and a teacher in a flood-prone district of Bihar are not the same credit profile, even if their salaries are identical. Know your geography.
Never sanction a loan that you would not personally be comfortable defending in an RBI audit. If the justification would make you uncomfortable in front of a regulator, the sanction is wrong.

The best customer acquisition strategy is also the best risk strategy: acquire customers who genuinely benefit from the loan, at a loan amount and tenor that is genuinely within their means, at a price that is genuinely fair. That borrower will repay not just this loan, but the next one too.
